artists.biography: Ride were a British shoegazing band that formed in 1988 in Oxford, England, consisting of Andy Bell, Mark Gardener, Laurence "Loz" Colbert, and Steve Queralt. The band were initially part of the "shoegazing" scene that emerged in England during the early 1990s. Following the break-up of the band in 1996, members moved on to various other projects, most notably Bell who became the bassist for Oasis. In 2001, the band members were briefly reunited for a one-off performance for a television show. Their debut album 'Nowhere' has been named one of the greatest albums of the shoegazing genre, Nowhere was voted number 74 on Pitchfork Media's list of the Top 100 Albums of the 1990s, and closing track "Vapour Trail" was voted at number 145 on Pitchfork's Top 200 Tracks of the 90s. The album is also included in the book '1001 Albums You Must Hear Before You Die'.

perplexity.description:
Going Blank Again" is the second studio album by British rock band Ride, originally released in March 1992 on Creation Records (not Wichita). Musically, the album marks a shift from the dense shoegaze textures of their debut, Nowhere, toward a broader sonic palette that incorporates elements of alternative rock, dream pop, and 1960s-influenced Britpop. The record features layered guitars, keyboards, acoustic passages, and even a sample from the film Withnail and I, showcasing the band’s expanding musical interests and willingness to experiment beyond the confines of their earlier sound.

Within Ride’s discography, "Going Blank Again" stands as a pivotal release that demonstrated their growth as songwriters and performers. It includes standout tracks such as "Leave Them All Behind," "Twisterella," and "OX4," which highlight the band’s ability to blend melodic hooks with atmospheric production. The album was well-received by critics for its ambition and stylistic range, cementing Ride’s reputation as one of the leading acts in the UK alternative rock scene. While not as commercially massive as some of their contemporaries, it achieved strong sales and critical acclaim, helping to define the evolving landscape of early 1990s British guitar music.
